spots.name: Christ Church Cathedral

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Christ Church Cathedral, previously spelled ChristChurch Cathedral and (rarely) called Cathedral Church of Christ, is a deconsecrated Anglican cathedral in the central city of Christchurch, New Zealand. It was built between 1864 and 1904 in the centre of the city, surrounded by Cathedral Square.

names.ja: クライストチャーチ大聖堂 (クライストチャーチ)
names.zh: 基督堂座堂 (克赖斯特彻奇)

spots.name: Christchurch Botanic Gardens
spots.summary: The Christchurch Botanic Gardens, located in the central city of Christchurch, New Zealand, were founded in 1863 when an English oak was planted to commemorate the solemnisation of the marriage of Prince Albert and Princess Alexandra of Denmark.

names.ja: クライストチャーチ植物園

spots.name: Hagley Park
spots.summary: Hagley Park is the largest urban open space in Christchurch, New Zealand, and was established in 1855 by the Provincial Government.

spots.name: Cathedral of the Blessed Sacrament

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Cathedral of the Blessed Sacrament, sometimes referred to as the Christchurch Basilica was a Catholic cathedral on Barbadoes Street in central Christchurch, New Zealand. It was the mother church of the Roman Catholic Diocese of Christchurch and seat of the Bishop of Christchurch.
spots.wikipediaTitle: Cathedral of the Blessed Sacrament, Christchurch

names.es: Catedral del Santísimo Sacramento de Christchurch
names.zh: 圣体主教座堂 (基督堂市)

spots.name: Canterbury Museum

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Canterbury Museum is a museum located in the central city of Christchurch, New Zealand, in the city's Cultural Precinct. The museum was established in 1867 with Julius von Haast – whose collection formed its core – as its first director.

spots.name: Cardboard Cathedral

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Cardboard Cathedral, formally called the Transitional Cathedral, in Christchurch, New Zealand, is the transitional pro-cathedral of the Anglican Diocese of Christchurch, replacing ChristChurch Cathedral, which was significantly damaged in the 2011 Christchurch earthquake.

spots.name: Cathedral Square
spots.summary: Cathedral Square, locally known simply as the Square, is the geographical centre and heart of Christchurch, New Zealand, where the city's Anglican cathedral, Christ Church Cathedral is located.

spots.name: Christchurch Art Gallery

hours.note: Closed Wed

spots.summary: The Christchurch Art Gallery is the public art gallery of the city of Christchurch, New Zealand. It has its own substantial art collection and also presents a programme of New Zealand and international exhibitions. It is funded by Christchurch City Council.

names.ja: クライストチャーチ美術館

spots.name: Christchurch Arts Centre
spots.summary: The Christchurch Arts Centre, also known as The Arts Centre Te Matatiki Toi Ora, is a hub for arts, culture, education, creativity and entrepreneurship in Christchurch, New Zealand.

names.ja: クライストチャーチ・アートセンター

spots.name: National Railway Museum of New Zealand

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The National Railway Museum of New Zealand (NRM) is a museum under construction in Christchurch, New Zealand, that covers the history of the New Zealand railway network. Work is underway to open at Ferrymead Heritage Park in Ferrymead, Christchurch, at the site of New Zealand's first railway opened in 1863.
spots.wikipediaTitle: National Railway Museum of New Zealand

names.fr: Musée national des chemins de fer de Nouvelle-Zélande

spots.name: Bridge of Remembrance
spots.summary: The Bridge of Remembrance is one of two main war memorials in Christchurch, New Zealand. It is dedicated to those who died in World War I, and serves as a memorial for those who participated in two World Wars as well as subsequent conflicts in Borneo, Korea, Malaya, and Vietnam.

spots.name: New Regent Street
spots.summary: New Regent Street is a pedestrian mall in Christchurch. Built as a private development in the early 1930s with 40 shops in Spanish Mission architectural style, it is one of the city's major tourist attractions.

spots.name: The Chalice
spots.summary: The Chalice is a sculpture in Cathedral Square, Christchurch, New Zealand. Designed by sculptor Neil Dawson, it was created to mark the 150th anniversary of the settlement of Canterbury, and installed in the square in 2001. The conical sculpture features the leaves of New Zealand native plants.

spots.name: Citizens' War Memorial
spots.summary: The Citizens' War Memorial in Cathedral Square, Christchurch, is one of the two major memorials in the city to World War I. It is located immediately north of ChristChurch Cathedral.

spots.name: Statue of Robert Falcon Scott
spots.summary: The Statue of Robert Falcon Scott, commonly known as the Scott Statue, is a statue in Christchurch, New Zealand commemorating British Antarctic explorer Robert Falcon Scott.
spots.wikipediaTitle: Statue of Robert Falcon Scott, Christchurch

spots.name: Christchurch Town Hall
spots.summary: The Christchurch Town Hall, since 2007 formally known as the Christchurch Town Hall of the Performing Arts, opened in 1972, is Christchurch, New Zealand's premier performing arts centre.

names.ja: クライストチャーチ・タウンホール

spots.name: Kate Sheppard National Memorial
spots.summary: The Kate Sheppard National Memorial, located in the city of Christchurch, is New Zealand's first memorial to the women's suffrage campaign, and particularly honours the life of one of the country's leading campaigners for women's suffrage, Kate Sheppard.

names.zh: 凯特·谢泼德国家纪念馆

spots.name: Peacock Fountain
spots.summary: The Peacock Fountain was bought by the Christchurch Beautifying Society from money bequeathed by John Thomas Peacock, a trader, politician and philanthropist. The fountain was unveiled in 1911, moved to a new location some years later, and put into storage in 1949.

spots.name: Victoria Square
spots.summary: Victoria Square is a public park located in central Christchurch, New Zealand. Originally known by European settlers as Market Place or Market Square, it was renamed to Victoria Square in 1903 in honour of Queen Victoria.

spots.name: Ferrymead Heritage Park
spots.summary: Ferrymead Heritage Park is an outdoor museum in Christchurch, New Zealand.

names.ja: フェリーミード歴史公園

spots.name: Firefighters Reserve
spots.summary: The Firefighters Reserve is a memorial in Christchurch, New Zealand, for the first responders during the September 11 attacks on the United States in 2001. The reserve contains the A Tribute to Firefighters monument, which has steel girders which were originally in the Twin Towers.

spots.name: Canterbury Provincial Council Buildings
spots.summary: The Canterbury Provincial Council Buildings are the buildings of the Canterbury Provincial Council that administered the Canterbury Province from 1853 until the abolition of provincial government in 1876. The buildings are the only purpose-built provincial government buildings in New Zealand still in existence.

spots.name: Twelve Local Heroes
spots.summary: The Twelve Local Heroes is a series of bronze busts in Christchurch, New Zealand. Sculpted by Mark Whyte, the objective was to commemorate twelve local Christchurch people who were prominent in their respective fields in the latter part of the 20th century.

spots.name: City Mall, Christchurch
spots.summary: City Mall is the main pedestrian mall in the central city of Christchurch, New Zealand, comprising two sections of Cashel Street plus the Bridge of Remembrance and one section of High Street. It is also known colloquially as Cashel Mall. The Bridge of Remembrance was pedestrianised in 1976.

spots.name: Air Force Museum of New Zealand
spots.summary: The Air Force Museum of New Zealand, formerly called The Royal New Zealand Air Force Museum, is located at Wigram, the RNZAF's first operational base, in Christchurch, in the South Island of New Zealand.
spots.wikipediaTitle: Air Force Museum of New Zealand

names.es: Museo de la Fuerza Aérea de Nueva Zelanda
names.ja: ニュージーランド空軍博物館

photo.author: Bernard Spragg. NZ from Christchurch, New Zealand

spots.name: Tūranga
spots.summary: Tūranga is the public library located in Central Christchurch, New Zealand. It opened on 12 October 2018 and replaced the nearby Christchurch Central Library that was closed on the day of the 2011 Christchurch earthquake.

spots.name: Christchurch Catholic Cathedral

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Cathedral of the Blessed Sacrament is the planned successor of Christchurch's former Catholic cathedral which was damaged in the 2010 and 2011 Canterbury earthquakes and later demolished in 2020. This makes the cathedral the future mother church of the Roman Catholic Diocese of Christchurch.

spots.name: Godley Statue
spots.summary: The Godley Statue is a bronze statue situated in Cathedral Square in Christchurch, New Zealand. It commemorates the "Founder of Canterbury" John Robert Godley. It was the first statue portraying a person in New Zealand.

spots.name: Diminish and Ascend
spots.summary: Diminish and Ascend is a welded aluminum stairway sculpture by David McCracken. It is permanently installed in the Christchurch Botanic Gardens in New Zealand. The sculpture is an optical illusion.

spots.name: Scorpio Books

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Scorpio Books is an independent bookstore in Christchurch, New Zealand. It was founded in 1976 by David Cameron, who changed the name of Pisces Books to match his and his wife Jane's astrological sign. Scorpio Books is one of the longest-running independent bookstores in New Zealand.

spots.name: Government Buildings (Former)
spots.summary: The Old Government Building is a heritage building complex in Christchurch, New Zealand. It was designed by Joseph Maddison in 1909 for use by government departments. It is a Category I heritage building listed with Heritage New Zealand.

photo.author: Bernard Spragg. NZ from Christchurch, New Zealand

spots.name: 185 chairs
spots.summary: 185 empty chairs, also known as 185 white chairs or 185 empty white chairs or simply as 185 chairs, was an unofficial memorial for the 185 individuals who died in the 2011 Christchurch earthquake.

spots.name: The Octagon

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Trinity Church or Trinity Congregational Church designed by Benjamin Mountfort, later called the State Trinity Centre, is a Category I heritage building listed with Heritage New Zealand.

photo.author: Trinity_Church,_Christchurch,_NZ.jpg: Robert Cutts derivative work: Schwede66

spots.name: Chief Post Office, Christchurch
spots.summary: The Chief Post Office or Christchurch Central Post Office, originally known as the Government Buildings, is located in Cathedral Square, Christchurch, New Zealand. The building was initially a post office with Immigration, Customs and Public Works departments.

spots.name: Robert McDougall Art Gallery

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Robert McDougall Art Gallery is a heritage building in Christchurch, New Zealand. It was designed by Edward Armstrong and it opened in 1932. It is a Category I heritage building listed with Heritage New Zealand and is located within the Christchurch Botanic Gardens.

spots.name: Ravenscar House Museum

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Ravenscar House Museum is an art museum located in Christchurch, New Zealand, and operated by Canterbury Museum. It exhibits the collection of Christchurch philanthropists and art collectors Jim and Susan Wakefield, and opened to the public on 8 November 2021.

spots.name: Fisher's Building
spots.summary: The Fisher's Building was a 19th-century Venetian Gothic building located in central Christchurch, New Zealand. It was designed in 1872 by architect William Armson and constructed from concrete and brick in 1880 on a central city site leased to Thomas Richard Fisher, who ran a tea and grocery store.

spots.name: Cook Statue
spots.summary: The Cook Statue in Victoria Square, Christchurch, commemorates the three journeys of James Cook to New Zealand. The statue was sculpted by William Trethewey and was unveiled on 10 August 1932 by the Governor-General, Lord Bledisloe. It was donated by bookmaker and philanthropist Matthew Barnett (1861–1935).

spots.name: Edmonds Band Rotunda
spots.summary: The Edmonds Band Rotunda is a rotunda in Christchurch, New Zealand. Created by baking powder manufacturer Thomas Edmonds in 1929 to celebrate his 50th year of living in the city, it was used initially as a place for brass bands to play music. It was converted to a restaurant in the 1980s.

spots.name: Our City, Christchurch
spots.summary: The Christchurch Municipal Chambers, previously known as Our City, is a Queen Anne style building on the corner of Worcester Street and Oxford Terrace in the Christchurch Central City. It is a Category I heritage building registered with Heritage New Zealand.

spots.name: Church of St Michael and All Angels

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Church of St Michael and All Angels is an Anglican church located at 84 Oxford Terrace, Christchurch, New Zealand.
spots.wikipediaTitle: Church of St Michael and All Angels, Christchurch

names.ru: Церковь Святого Михаила и Всех Ангелов (Крайстчерч)

spots.name: Worcester Street
spots.summary: Worcester Street is a road in the central city of Christchurch, New Zealand. It runs from the intersection of Rolleston Avenue in the west, and terminates in the east at the intersection of Woodham Road in Linwood. Between Rolleston Avenue and Cambridge Terrace, it is known as Worcester Boulevard.

spots.name: Shand's Emporium
spots.summary: Shand's Emporium, previously known as Gee's, is a historic building in the central city of Christchurch, New Zealand.

spots.name: Rolleston Statue
spots.summary: The Rolleston Statue is a white marble statue situated outside Canterbury Museum on Rolleston Avenue in Christchurch, New Zealand. It commemorates William Rolleston, who was Superintendent of the Canterbury Province from 1868 until 1877.

spots.name: Canterbury Earthquake National Memorial
spots.summary: The Canterbury Earthquake National Memorial is the Crown's official memorial for those killed or seriously injured in the 22 February 2011 Christchurch earthquake. It is located on both sides of the Avon River / Ōtākaro downstream from the Montreal Street bridge.

spots.name: Christ's College Chapel

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Christ's College Chapel is part of Christ's College, Christchurch.

spots.name: Christchurch Adventure Park
spots.summary: Christchurch Adventure Park is an adventure park in the Port Hills of Christchurch, New Zealand. Built by the Canadian company Select Evolution, it had its opening function on 16 December 2016. The 1500 holders of special passes could ride from 17 December, while the park opened to the public on 21 December.

spots.name: Christchurch Club
spots.summary: The Christchurch Club is a historic private members' club in the central city of Christchurch, New Zealand. The older of the two Christchurch clubs, it was founded by rural landholders in 1856; the rival organisation, the Canterbury Club, was a breakaway that was founded by urban professionals in 1872.

spots.name: Public Trust Building, Christchurch
spots.summary: The former Public Trust Building in Christchurch, New Zealand, is a heritage building designed by leading architect Cecil Wood that was threatened with demolition. It is now being restored for a range of office and hospitality tenants.

spots.name: Beth El Synagogue
spots.summary: The Beth El Synagogue was a Jewish congregation and synagogue, that was located at 78 Gloucester Street, in Christchurch, New Zealand. The first structure, a wooden synagogue, was completed in 1864. It was replaced by a stone building in 1881. The synagogue was demolished in 1987.

spots.name: Hamish Hay Bridge
spots.summary: Hamish Hay Bridge is a bridge located in Victoria Square, Christchurch, New Zealand. Built in 1864, it was renamed in 1989 for Sir Hamish Hay, Mayor of Christchurch; a commemorative bronze plaque is affixed to the bridge's guard rail in the middle of the structure to honor Hay's services.

spots.name: Canterbury Club
spots.summary: The Canterbury Club is a historic gentlemen's club in the central city of Christchurch, New Zealand. It was founded by urban professionals in 1872 as a breakaway club from the Christchurch Club, which had been set up by large rural landholders in 1856.

spots.name: Weston House
spots.summary: Weston House was a substantial two-storey heritage building in Christchurch, New Zealand, designed by architect Cecil Wood in Neo-Georgian style for George Weston, and completed in 1924. Registered as a Category I heritage building since 1983, it was demolished after the 2011 Christchurch earthquake.

spots.name: Statue of Queen Victoria
spots.summary: The statue of Queen Victoria is a large bronze statue of Queen Victoria in Victoria Square, Christchurch. It was sculpted by British artist Francis John Williamson and erected in 1903.

spots.name: St John the Baptist Church, Christchurch

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: St John the Baptist Church is a former Anglican church that was located in Latimer Square, Christchurch, New Zealand.
spots.wikipediaTitle: St John the Baptist Church, Christchurch

spots.name: Latimer Square
spots.summary: Latimer Square is an urban park in central Christchurch, New Zealand. It is located 400 metres (440 yd) east of the city's centre, Cathedral Square. Many commemorative events take place in Latimer Square. The square lies between the major urban thoroughfares of Gloucester Street and Worcester Street.

spots.name: Oxford Terrace Baptist Church

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Oxford Terrace Baptist Church is a Baptist church located in the Christchurch Central City on a prominent corner property fronting the Avon River. It is affiliated with the Baptist Churches of New Zealand.

spots.name: Christchurch Central Library

hours.note: Closed Sun; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Canterbury Public Library building, was a library in Central Christchurch and the main library of Christchurch City Libraries, New Zealand. It was the largest library in the South Island and the third-biggest in New Zealand. It was also known as the Central Library.

spots.name: Armagh Street Bridge
spots.summary: The Armagh Street Bridge is a historic bridge on Armagh Street in Christchurch Central City. It sits between the Convention Centre Precinct and the Magistrate's Court at the south-west corner of Victoria Square.

spots.name: Curator's House
spots.summary: The Curator's House is a historic building in the Christchurch Botanic Garden, in Christchurch, New Zealand. It was built for the Curator of the Botanic Gardens in 1920 and it is now home to a restaurant, called The Curator's House.

spots.name: Quake City
spots.summary: Coordinated by Canterbury Museum, it has exhibits about earthquakes in Christchurch, particularly the quakes of 2010–11.

spots.name: Site of Canterbury Television building
spots.summary: The site of the CTV building, where 115 people died was planted as a memorial garden in 2018.

spots.name: Tramway Restaurant

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Have a seasonal dinner in a moving tramcar and enjoy sightseeing central Christchurch outside the windows. Gluten-free, dairy-free, vegetarian, vegan and halal options available. Duration: 2.5 hours (an airplane-style restroom is available in the tramcar). Reservations (via phone or online or at Christchurch Attractions inside Cathedral Junction) are required.

spots.name: Afghan Restaurant
spots.summary: A rustic place that offers tasty chicken or lamb cooked over an open flame grill, served with rice and salad. A chicken curry is usually available too. Large portions, and you can takeout any leftovers. There is no menu and no toilet on site.

spots.name: Dux Dine

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Pescatarian restaurant with lovely garden seating, the pizzas are good value to share, and the salads are fantastic. Also serves their craft beers including alcoholic ginger beer. One half of the erstwhile Dux de Lux in Hereford St.

spots.name: Holy Smoke

hours.note: Closed Mon, Sun

spots.summary: Deli specialising in food that has been manuka-smoked in house. The smoked salmon alone is well worth the trip. (No longer has a restaurant.)

spots.name: No. 4

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Bar and restaurant. Relaxed during the day and busy (but not too busy) on weekend nights. Great wines, Monteiths beers and a solid menu.

spots.name: Strawberry Fare

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Carries an extensive menu of modern interpreted New Zealand dishes and many dessert dishes. Reservations are required.

spots.name: Pak'n'Save
spots.summary: The cheapest supermarket chain overall, but may not have as wide a range as Woolworths and New World.

spots.name: Under the Red Verandah
spots.summary: Offers a range of food incorporating fair trade coffee, free range eggs and gluten-free baked goods.

spots.name: Welcome

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Delicious Chinese vegetarian meals. Don't miss the hotplate and clay pot special dishes too!

spots.name: Addington Coffee Co-Op

hours.note: Closed Sun

spots.summary: Sells fair trade coffee and clothing in a lively atmosphere. Also has a laundry.

spots.name: Fresh Choice

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The most central supermarket, but also the smallest, and not the cheapest.

spots.name: @Tony's
spots.summary: Good Japanese teppanyaki with special all-you-can-eat deals Su-Th ($42).

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: A relaxed atmosphere bar, a great place for meals.

spots.summary: An upscale bistro and bar in trendy Merivale.

spots.summary: Fresh fruit and vegetables and some meat.
